title: Container and Raw Buffer Out-of-Bounds
platform_conditions: C++11 and later on any conforming toolchain; operator[] is unchecked by default in release, and only libstdc++/MSVC debug builds assert
security_mechanism: vector::operator[] and string::operator[] perform no bounds check in conforming release builds: the standard makes an out-of-range index undefined behavior rather than an exception, so an attacker-supplied index reads or writes whatever object lies at data() + i * element_size. The same unchecked boundary appears where C++ hands its buffer to C: passing vector::data() plus a separately-tracked length to a C API lets a stale or mismatched length parameter overflow the vector's allocation, since data() itself is a raw pointer carrying no size.

source_sink_clues.source: Indexes and lengths from protocol fields, request parameters, parsed message offsets, or computed from attacker-influenced values.
source_sink_clues.sink: operator[] on vector/deque/string/map with an unchecked index; data()/c_str() plus an external length handed to memcpy or a C API

tracking_guards: Check that .at() is used (throws std::out_of_range) or the index is explicitly compared against .size() before operator[], and that every data()-plus-length hand-off to C derives both from the same container object in the same expression (size() called on the live vector, not a cached value).
not_candidate_when: The index was validated against size() on the same path before the access, the container is a compile-time array with a constant index, or the buffer is only passed to C interfaces with lengths derived from the same live container object.
public_references: CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/129.html
C++ Core Guidelines: ES (expressions and statements) — https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines
